articles.title: Pet First | 6 Things Your Dog Does That Actually Mean They Trust You
articles.description:
Dogs may not be able to tell us how they feel in words, but their behaviour can reveal a lot about their comfort and bond with the people around them. Trust develops gradually when a dog feels safe, respected and cared for. From relaxing around you to seeking you out when they need reassurance, certain everyday behaviours can be signs that your dog feels secure in your presence. However, every dog has a different personality. A behaviour should always be understood in the context of the dog's overall body language and usual habits.

They Relax Completely Around You

A dog that feels safe may become noticeably relaxed in your presence. They might stretch out, rest comfortably or even fall asleep nearby. Dogs are naturally alert to their surroundings, so being able to settle down around someone can indicate that they feel comfortable. If your dog regularly chooses to rest near you without appearing tense or fearful, it can be a positive sign of familiarity and trust.

They Follow You Around The House

Does your dog seem to appear wherever you go? Following you from one room to another can simply mean they enjoy your company. Dogs are social animals and often stay close to people they have formed strong bonds with. While following you does not automatically mean trust, consistently choosing to remain near you can indicate that your dog associates you with safety and companionship.

ALSO READ | Pet First | 6 Signs Your Dog Is Bored At Home And Needs More Mental Stimulation

They Sleep Near You

Sleep is a vulnerable state for animals. When a dog chooses to sleep beside you or in the same room, it may indicate that they feel comfortable enough to relax in your presence. Some dogs prefer their own space, so sleeping elsewhere does not mean they distrust you. What matters is whether they appear relaxed wherever they choose to sleep.

They Bring Their Favourite Toys

If your dog brings you a favourite toy, they may be inviting you to interact or play. In some cases, dogs also carry toys to people they are comfortable around simply because they associate them with positive experiences. Rather than focusing only on the object, look at the dog's overall behaviour—such as a relaxed posture, playful movements and willingness to stay close.

ALSO READ | Pet First | Kitten Weaning Guide: When And How To Start Solid Food

They Seek You Out When They're Unsure

Dogs may look toward or move closer to a trusted person when something unfamiliar happens. If your dog comes to you during a noisy situation or when encountering something new, it can suggest that they see you as a source of reassurance. Give them space rather than forcing interaction, especially if they appear anxious.

They Maintain A Relaxed Body Around You

A dog's body language can be one of the clearest indicators of comfort. Soft facial expressions, a loose body, natural movements and an easygoing posture generally suggest that the dog is relaxed. Trust is built through consistent care, patience and respecting boundaries. Rather than expecting affection on demand, allowing your dog to approach you freely can help strengthen the bond over time.
